passages.title: Two Hours Outside a Tunnel
passages.passage: Last Sunday my aunt and I took the early train to visit my grandparents, who live in a small town about three hours (1)____ the coast. We arrived at the station in plenty (2)____ time and found our seats easily. The train left at exactly seven, and for the first hour everything went smoothly. Then, just outside a tunnel, it slowed (3)____ and finally stopped. At first nobody was worried, but after twenty minutes people began to look at their watches. A voice announced that a tree had fallen across the line and that the delay would last (4)____ least an hour. My aunt, who hates waiting, was about to complain to the guard (5)____ she noticed a little boy crying in the next row. His mother had run out of snacks, so my aunt took (6)____ a packet of biscuits and offered him one. Soon the whole carriage was sharing food and telling stories, and I forgot all (7)____ the time. When the train finally moved again, a few passengers even looked disappointed. We reached my grandparents' house two hours late, (8)____ my grandmother had kept our lunch warm. Looking back, I think that afternoon taught me something useful: a delay is only as bad (9)____ you let it be. If I had spent those two hours complaining, I (10)____ never have met the friendly people around me.

questions.q: Blank (1): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Distance or travel time is measured from a place: three hours from the coast. Of, at and by cannot express how far away something is.

questions.q: Blank (2): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is in plenty of time (early enough). Plenty is always followed by of before a noun.

questions.q: Blank (3): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb slow down means to go more slowly. Slow up, slow off and slow out are not used for a vehicle losing speed.

questions.q: Blank (4): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: At least means 'not less than': at least an hour. The other prepositions do not combine with least in this meaning.

questions.q: Blank (5): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Was about to do something when describes an action that was interrupted at the last moment. While needs a longer, continuing action, and after or since would change the order of events.

questions.q: Blank (6): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Take out means to remove something from a bag or pocket. Take off is for clothes or planes, take up is for hobbies, and take over means to gain control.

questions.q: Blank (7): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: You forget about something when it goes out of your mind for a while. Forget of/for/with are not English collocations.

questions.q: Blank (8): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Arriving late and still finding lunch warm are a contrast, so but is needed. So and because would make the warm lunch a result or a reason for being late.

questions.q: Blank (9): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The comparison of equality is as + adjective + as: only as bad as you let it be. Than follows a comparative such as worse, which is not used here.

questions.q: Blank (10): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: This is a third conditional: If I had spent…, I would never have met…. Will belongs to the first conditional, and had or was cannot come before have met.

passages.title: A Stadium Full of Stars
passages.passage: I had been saving my pocket money for months, so when my cousin offered me a ticket to see my favourite band, I could hardly believe my luck. The concert was held (1)____ a Saturday evening in the big stadium near the river. We set (2)____ early because my cousin said the queue would be enormous, and she was right. Thousands of fans were already waiting, many of (3)____ were wearing the band's T-shirt. While we stood in line, a girl behind us explained that she had travelled all the way from another province (4)____ her own. I remember thinking how brave that was. When the gates finally opened, everybody rushed forward, and I nearly lost my cousin in the crowd. Inside, the noise was (5)____ loud that I could not hear myself speak. The band came on stage at eight o'clock sharp, and from the first note the whole stadium seemed to move together. I sang (6)____ to every song, even the ones I did not know well. Halfway through, the singer stopped and asked the audience to turn on their phone lights, (7)____ turned the stadium into a sky full of stars. I have never seen anything (8)____ it. By the end, my voice had almost disappeared and my feet hurt, but I did not care. On the way home my cousin asked whether I had enjoyed it. I told her it was the best night (9)____ my life, and I meant it. I am already saving (10)____ for the next one.

questions.q: Blank (1): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Days and parts of a named day take on: on a Saturday evening. In is used with the evening alone, and at with clock times.

questions.q: Blank (2): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Set off means to start a journey. Set up means to establish or prepare something, and set away or set down do not describe leaving.

questions.q: Blank (3): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: After a preposition in a relative clause about people, the pronoun is whom: many of whom. Them would create two sentences joined by a comma, and which is for things.

questions.q: Blank (4): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The phrase for 'alone' is on her own. By would need herself (by herself), not her own.

questions.q: Blank (5): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: So + adjective + that expresses a result: so loud that I could not hear. Such needs a noun, and too or very cannot be followed by a that clause.

questions.q: Blank (6): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Sing along to a song means to sing together with the music. Sing on, sing out and sing away are not followed by to every song.

questions.q: Blank (7): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Which after a comma refers back to the whole previous idea (asking everyone to turn on their lights). That cannot follow a comma in this way, and it would need a new sentence.

questions.q: Blank (8): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Anything like it means anything similar to it. As would need to be paired with an adjective, and than needs a comparative.

questions.q: Blank (9): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: A superlative is usually followed by of plus the group or period: the best night of my life. At, for and to do not link a superlative to my life.

questions.q: Blank (10): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Save up for something means to keep money aside until you can buy it. Save on means to spend less on something, which is not the meaning here.

passages.title: The Cat Who Belongs to Everyone
passages.passage: Nobody in our street knows (1)____ the grey cat really belongs to. He appeared about two years ago, thin and nervous, and at first he ran away (2)____ soon as anyone came near. Mrs Hoa at number twelve started leaving a bowl of rice and fish by her gate, and little (3)____ little he became braver. These days he behaves as if he owns the whole neighbourhood. In the morning he sits on the wall outside the bakery, waiting (4)____ the baker to drop a piece of bread. At lunchtime he can usually be found asleep under the motorbike that belongs to the man who mends shoes. My little brother (5)____ to him as Captain, although the children next door call him something completely different. Last winter he disappeared for almost a week, and everybody started asking (6)____ another about him. My mother even put a notice on the lamp post. Then one evening he simply walked back through our gate, looking rather pleased with (7)____. We still have no idea where he had been. Some neighbours say he is a nuisance because he chases the birds, (8)____ most of us would miss him terribly if he left. A cat that belongs to nobody, it seems, ends up belonging (9)____ everyone. I sometimes wonder whether he would stay if one family finally decided to keep him inside. Something tells me he (10)____ rather keep his freedom.

questions.q: Blank (1): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The cat belongs to a person, so the question word is who: who the cat belongs to. Which and what are for things, and whose would need a noun after it.

questions.q: Blank (2): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The linker is as soon as, meaning immediately after. So soon as is not modern English, and too or very cannot join two clauses.

questions.q: Blank (3): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Little by little means gradually, in small steps, like one by one or day by day. The other prepositions do not form this expression.

questions.q: Blank (4): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The pattern is wait for somebody to do something. Wait to is followed directly by a verb, not by a person.

questions.q: Blank (5): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Only refer to somebody as takes both to and as. Calls and names would be followed directly by the name, with no to … as.

questions.q: Blank (6): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: One another means each person asked the others. Each pairs with other (each other), not with another.

questions.q: Blank (7): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The subject and the object are the same cat, so a reflexive pronoun is needed, and the passage calls the cat he: pleased with himself. Itself does not match he.

questions.q: Blank (8): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Calling him a nuisance and saying people would miss him are opposite ideas, so but joins them. So and because would wrongly make one idea the result or cause of the other.

questions.q: Blank (9): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The verb pattern is belong to somebody, as in the first sentence of the passage. Belong with exists but means 'fit naturally with', not ownership.

questions.q: Blank (10): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Preference is expressed with would rather + bare verb: he would rather keep his freedom. Should and could do not combine with rather in this meaning.

passages.title: The Friday Puzzle
passages.passage: Every Friday our maths teacher, Mr Tuan, writes a puzzle on the board before the lesson ends. Anyone (1)____ solves it by Monday gets a small prize, usually a pencil or a sticker. Last week's puzzle looked simple: three friends bought a cake for ninety thousand dong and paid thirty thousand each. Later the shop gave five thousand back, and they kept one thousand each and gave the last two thousand to the waiter. Mr Tuan asked us to explain (2)____ the numbers did not seem to add up. At first I was sure I could solve it (3)____ ten minutes. I wrote the numbers down, added them, and (4)____ added them again. Each time I got the same confusing result, and I started to feel annoyed (5)____ myself. On Saturday I gave up and went to play football. But on Sunday evening, (6)____ I was brushing my teeth, the answer suddenly appeared in my head. I had been adding the wrong things together! The waiter's two thousand had already come (7)____ of the money the friends paid, so it should not be counted twice. I ran to my desk and wrote the explanation out neatly. On Monday I handed it in, and Mr Tuan smiled and gave me a blue pencil. He said that most people fail not (8)____ the puzzle is difficult, but because they trust the first idea they have. (9)____ then I have tried to check my first idea before I believe it. The pencil, by the way, has already been lost, (10)____ the lesson has not.

questions.q: Blank (1): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The relative pronoun is the subject of solves and refers to a person, so it must be who. Whom is only for objects, and which is for things.

questions.q: Blank (2): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The teacher wants the reason, so the indirect question begins with why. What, which and whom would need a missing noun or object in the clause, and there is none.

questions.q: Blank (3): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The time needed to finish a task is expressed with in: solve it in ten minutes. For ten minutes describes how long an activity lasts, not how quickly it is completed.

questions.q: Blank (4): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Then shows the next step in a sequence: added them, and then added them again. Than belongs to comparisons, and after would need an object or a clause.

questions.q: Blank (5): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: You are annoyed with a person, including yourself. Annoyed by introduces the thing that causes the feeling, which is not the meaning here.

questions.q: Blank (6): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: While introduces a clause describing a longer action in progress. During is followed by a noun, never by a subject and verb, and until or since would change the meaning.

questions.q: Blank (7): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Come out of means to be taken from a sum of money. Come off, come up and come away are not followed by of the money in this sense.

questions.q: Blank (8): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The structure not because … but because … needs the same linker in both halves. Since and as cannot follow not in this contrast, and though gives the wrong meaning.

questions.q: Blank (9): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: Since then goes with the present perfect have tried to show something that started in the past and continues. From then would need on, and after or until do not match the tense.

questions.q: Blank (10): choose the word that fits.
questions.explanation: The pencil is lost and the lesson is not — a contrast, so but is required. So and because would suggest a cause-and-effect link that does not exist.

passages.title: The Watch at the Top of the Hill
passages.passage: On my fourteenth birthday my father announced that, instead (1)____ a party, we were going to climb the hill behind our town. I was not keen at first, because I had wanted to spend the day (2)____ my friends. However, he promised that the view from the top would be worth the effort, so I agreed. We set off at six, before the sun (3)____ even risen, carrying a bag of bread, bananas and cold water. The path was steep and muddy in places, and twice I slipped and nearly fell. My father, (4)____ walks in the hills every weekend, did not slip once. He kept stopping to point out birds and plants (5)____ I had never noticed before, even though I had lived below this hill all my life. After about two hours we reached the top (6)____ last, and we sat down on a flat rock to eat. He was right about the view. The whole town lay below us, so small that I could cover our house with one finger. I had never seen it (7)____ that. Then my father took a small box out of his bag. Inside was a watch that had belonged (8)____ my grandfather. He said he had been waiting (9)____ I was old enough to look after it. (10)____ I have had many presents in my life, none of them has meant as much as that one. Now I want to climb the hill every birthday.

questions.q: Blank (1): type ONE word.
questions.explanation: The fixed phrase is instead of + noun: instead of a party. Instead on its own can only end a clause, and rather would need than, not a single word.

questions.q: Blank (2): type ONE word.
questions.explanation: You spend time with people. Spend the day for my friends would mean doing it for their benefit, and among is not used for a small group of friends.

questions.q: Blank (3): type ONE word.
questions.explanation: Risen is a past participle, so it needs had to form the past perfect: the sun rising happened later than setting off. Has is present perfect and does not fit a past narrative, and was would need rising.

questions.q: Blank (4): type ONE word.
questions.explanation: The clause between commas gives extra information about a person and is the subject of walks, so it takes who. That is not used in non-defining clauses after a comma, and whom is only for objects.

questions.q: Blank (5): type ONE word.
questions.explanation: Birds and plants are things and the object of noticed, so the defining relative pronoun is that or which. Who is only for people, and what cannot follow a noun.

questions.q: Blank (6): type ONE word.
questions.explanation: At last means finally, after a long time. In the end and finally exist, but in last or by last do not.

questions.q: Blank (7): type ONE word.
questions.explanation: Like that means in that way or from that view. As that is not used with a pronoun in this sense, and such would need a noun.

questions.q: Blank (8): type ONE word.
questions.explanation: The verb pattern is belong to somebody. Belong with means 'fit naturally alongside', which is not about ownership.

questions.q: Blank (9): type ONE word.
questions.explanation: Wait until (or till) + clause means waiting up to the moment something becomes true. Wait for must be followed by a noun, not by I was old enough.

questions.q: Blank (10): type ONE word.
questions.explanation: The first clause admits a fact and the second contrasts with it, so a concession linker such as Although (or Though, While) is needed. But and however cannot introduce a clause that comes before the comma in this way.
